title: Deploy to Azure Container Apps with CI/CD
description: Build a Docker image of a FastAPI app, push it to Azure Container Registry, deploy it to Azure Container Apps, and set up a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline.
objective: Students will learn to containerize a FastAPI application with Docker, push the image to Azure Container Registry, deploy it to Azure Container Apps, set up a GitHub Actions workflow for automated deployment, and verify the deployment with monitoring.

steps.title: Set Up Azure and Install Tools
steps.instructions:
Before we deploy to Azure, we need an Azure account and the Azure CLI tool installed on our computer.

**Step A:** Create a free Azure account:
1. Go to [azure.microsoft.com/free](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-in/free/)
2. Click **Start free**
3. Sign in with your Microsoft account (or create one)
4. You will get **₹13,500 free credits** valid for 30 days — more than enough for this lab!
5. After sign-up, visit [portal.azure.com](https://portal.azure.com) — this is your Azure dashboard

**Step B:** Install Azure CLI:

For **Windows**:
```bash
# Download and run the installer from:
# https://aka.ms/installazurecliwindows
# OR use winget:
winget install Microsoft.AzureCLI
```

For **Mac/Linux**:
```bash
curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | sudo bash
```

**Step C:** Log into Azure from your terminal:
```bash
az login
```
This will open a browser window — sign in with the same account you used for the free tier.

**Step D:** Verify the login:
```bash
# Check your account details
az account show --query "{name:name, id:id, state:state}" -o table
```

You should see your subscription name and "Enabled" state.

**Step E:** Install Docker Desktop:
1. Download from [docker.com/products/docker-desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
2. Install and restart your computer
3. Verify: `docker --version` should print a version number

**Checkpoint:** You can run `az login`, `docker --version`, and see your Azure subscription.

steps.title: Create a Dockerfile and Build the Image
steps.instructions:
Docker packages your app into a "container" — a box that has everything your app needs to run. This box works the same way on your laptop, on Azure, and anywhere else.

**Step A:** Make sure your FastAPI project is ready. Use the same project from Lab 15-A or create this structure:

```
techpath-api/
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   └── main.py
├── requirements.txt
├── .dockerignore
└── Dockerfile
```

**Step B:** Create a `Dockerfile` in your project root:

```dockerfile
# Use an official Python image as the base
# "slim" means a smaller image (faster to build and deploy)
FROM python:3.12-slim

# Set the working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy ONLY requirements first (Docker caches this layer)
# This means if your code changes but dependencies don't,
# Docker skips re-installing packages — saves 2-3 minutes!
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Now copy the rest of your code
COPY . .

# Tell Docker which port your app uses
EXPOSE 8000

# Start the app when the container runs
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

**Step C:** Create a `.dockerignore` file (like .gitignore but for Docker):

```
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.env
.env.local
venv/
*.db
.git/
.github/
```

**Step D:** Build the Docker image locally:

```bash
# Build the image and tag it as "techpath-api"
docker build -t techpath-api:v1 .

# Run it locally to test
docker run -p 8000:8000 techpath-api:v1
```

Visit `http://localhost:8000/health` — if it works in Docker locally, it will work on Azure!

Press `Ctrl+C` to stop the container.

**Checkpoint:** `docker build` completes without errors, and your app runs in a container locally.

steps.title: Create Azure Resources and Push Image
steps.instructions:
Now we create the Azure resources we need: a Resource Group (folder), a Container Registry (image warehouse), and push our Docker image to it.

**Step A:** Create a Resource Group:
```bash
# A Resource Group is like a folder that holds all your Azure resources
az group create \
  --name techpath-rg \
  --location centralindia
```

**Step B:** Create an Azure Container Registry (ACR):
```bash
# ACR stores your Docker images in the cloud
# The name must be globally unique — add your initials or a number
az acr create \
  --name techpathregistry \
  --resource-group techpath-rg \
  --sku Basic \
  --admin-enabled true
```

**Step C:** Log into ACR from your terminal:
```bash
az acr login --name techpathregistry
```

**Step D:** Tag your local image for ACR:
```bash
# Format: <registry-url>/<image-name>:<tag>
docker tag techpath-api:v1 techpathregistry.azurecr.io/techpath-api:v1
```

**Step E:** Push the image to ACR:
```bash
docker push techpathregistry.azurecr.io/techpath-api:v1
```
This uploads your Docker image to Azure. It takes 1-3 minutes depending on your internet speed.

**Step F:** Verify the image is in ACR:
```bash
az acr repository list --name techpathregistry -o table
```
You should see `techpath-api` in the list.

**Step G:** Create a Container Apps Environment:
```bash
# The environment is a shared space where your container apps run
az containerapp env create \
  --name techpath-env \
  --resource-group techpath-rg \
  --location centralindia
```

**Checkpoint:** Your Docker image is in Azure Container Registry, and the Container Apps environment is ready.

steps.title: Deploy to Container Apps and Set Up GitHub Actions
steps.instructions:
Now we deploy the container and set up automatic deployments with GitHub Actions.

**Step A:** Deploy to Azure Container Apps:
```bash
az containerapp create \
  --name techpath-api \
  --resource-group techpath-rg \
  --environment techpath-env \
  --image techpathregistry.azurecr.io/techpath-api:v1 \
  --target-port 8000 \
  --ingress external \
  --registry-server techpathregistry.azurecr.io \
  --query "properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn" \
  --output tsv
```

This command outputs your app's public URL — something like:
`techpath-api.happyriver-abc123.centralindia.azurecontainerapps.io`

Visit `https://<your-url>/health` in your browser to verify it works!

**Step B:** Create a Service Principal for GitHub Actions:
```bash
# This creates a "robot account" that GitHub can use to deploy to Azure
SUB_ID=$(az account show --query id -o tsv)

az ad sp create-for-rbac \
  --name "github-techpath-deploy" \
  --role contributor \
  --scopes /subscriptions/$SUB_ID/resourceGroups/techpath-rg \
  --json-auth
```

**Save the entire JSON output** — you will need it in the next step.

**Step C:** Add GitHub Secrets:
1. Go to your GitHub repo → **Settings** → **Secrets and variables** → **Actions**
2. Click **New repository secret** and add these:

| Secret Name | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` | The entire JSON from Step B |
| `REGISTRY_LOGIN_SERVER` | `techpathregistry.azurecr.io` |
| `REGISTRY_USERNAME` | Run: `az acr credential show --name techpathregistry --query username -o tsv` |
| `REGISTRY_PASSWORD` | Run: `az acr credential show --name techpathregistry --query "passwords[0].value" -o tsv` |

**Step D:** Create the GitHub Actions workflow file:
1. In your project, create the folder: `.github/workflows/`
2. Create a file `.github/workflows/deploy-azure.yml`
3. Copy the workflow from the `code-azure-container-deploy.yml` file in this module
4. Update the `env` section with your actual resource names

**Step E:** Push the workflow to GitHub:
```bash
git add .github/workflows/deploy-azure.yml
git commit -m "Add Azure Container Apps deployment workflow"
git push origin main
```

Go to your GitHub repo → **Actions** tab — you should see the workflow running!

**Checkpoint:** Your app is live on Azure Container Apps, and the GitHub Actions workflow runs when you push to main.

steps.title: Verify Deployment and Set Up Monitoring
steps.instructions:
The app is deployed! Now let us verify everything works and set up basic monitoring so we know if it goes down.

**Step A:** Test all endpoints on Azure:

Replace `<your-url>` with your actual Container Apps URL:

```
https://<your-url>/              → Welcome message
https://<your-url>/health         → Health check JSON
https://<your-url>/docs           → Swagger documentation
https://<your-url>/api/v1/students → Sample student data
```

All four should return valid JSON responses.

**Step B:** Check container logs in Azure:
```bash
# View real-time logs from your running container
az containerapp logs show \
  --name techpath-api \
  --resource-group techpath-rg \
  --follow
```

You should see uvicorn startup logs and incoming HTTP requests. Press `Ctrl+C` to stop.

**Step C:** Set up uptime monitoring with UptimeRobot:
1. Go to [uptimerobot.com](https://uptimerobot.com) and create a free account
2. Click **Add New Monitor**
3. Fill in:
   - **Monitor Type:** HTTP(s)
   - **Friendly Name:** TechPath API (Azure)
   - **URL:** `https://<your-url>/health`
   - **Monitoring Interval:** 5 minutes
4. Add your email for alerts
5. Click **Create Monitor**

Now if your app goes down, you get an email within 5 minutes!

**Step D:** Test the CI/CD pipeline end-to-end:
1. Make a small change in `app/main.py` (e.g., change the version to "2.0.0")
2. Commit and push:
```bash
git add app/main.py
git commit -m "Bump version to test CI/CD pipeline"
git push origin main
```
3. Go to GitHub → Actions tab → watch the deployment run
4. After it finishes (3-5 minutes), visit your Azure URL — the change should be live

**Step E:** Document your work. Take screenshots of:
1. Azure Portal showing your Container App running
2. The `/health` endpoint response from the Azure URL
3. GitHub Actions showing a successful deployment (green checkmark)
4. UptimeRobot dashboard with your monitor
5. Container logs from Azure CLI

**Final Checklist:**

| Item | Done? |
|------|-------|
| Docker image built and pushed to ACR | |
| Container App running on Azure | |
| All endpoints accessible via HTTPS | |
| GitHub Actions workflow runs on push | |
| UptimeRobot monitoring set up | |
| CI/CD pipeline tested end-to-end | |

**Congratulations!** You have set up a professional-grade deployment pipeline. This is the same approach companies like TechPath Institute use to deploy their production applications across data centres in Mumbai and Delhi!
